class_name MouseLock
extends RefCounted

## The browser's pointer lock, the real one. Godot asks for the lock itself from its main loop (not
## inside the click), and in some browsers (Opera, a cooldown after Esc, an unfocused tab) it is
## never granted or is lost, while Godot still reports mouse_mode CAPTURED and the free cursor's
## movementX keeps turning the camera until the cursor hits the screen edge ("a wall"). So:
## - a JS listener on the page asks canvas.requestPointerLock() INSIDE the pointerdown/mousedown
##   gesture (unadjustedMovement first, plain on NotSupportedError, one retry after the Esc cooldown);
## - the look turns ONLY while held() (the browser really holds the lock); when it is lost the game
##   sets mouse_mode VISIBLE at once (the click-to-play card shows), the next click relocks.
## Off the web held() is just mouse_mode == CAPTURED. `ui_open`: a panel owns the mouse (no lock asked).

# Mouse bug ("camera freezes as if the cursor hit a wall", Opera) and movement numbers

## Diagnosis
Godot web: `GodotDisplayCursor.lockPointer()` calls `canvas.requestPointerLock()` from the engine main loop, not from
inside the DOM click handler, and mouse motion is delivered from window `pointermove` (`evt.movementX`) whether or not the
lock is held. Old game code: click -> `Input.mouse_mode = CAPTURED` -> turn whenever `mouse_mode == CAPTURED`.
If the browser never grants the lock (request outside the gesture / after the transient activation expired / Opera's own
policy / Esc cooldown / lost focus), Godot still says CAPTURED, the *free* cursor's movementX keeps turning the camera,
and it stops dead when the cursor reaches the screen edge (movementX = 0 there): "as if the cursor hit a wall". This is the
most likely cause; it could not be reproduced in Opera here (no Opera on the hub), only Chrome (Chromium, same engine).
Also: Godot's CAPTURED state was never corrected when the lock was lost (Esc is eaten by the browser, the game never sees it).

## Browser facts (sources)
- A lock request needs transient user activation (a click/key), and fails right after the user's own Esc exit:
  MDN https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API​/Element/requestPointerLock and
  https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Pointer_Lock_API
- Chromium refuses a re-lock for ~1.2

Swing (world/chop/axe_swing.gd, AxeSwing, pure and deterministic):
- The head travels on a circle about the shoulder; crouching lowers the shoulder by Actor.CROUCH_DROP (binary meta, same on server, pilot and bots). A one-hand left swing uses the left shoulder and mirrors the direction.
- The swing plane is spanned by shoulder→aim point and the camera right axis, turned by InputSystem.swing_of (wheel, 15° steps).
- Radius = distance to what the look meets + DRIVE 4 cm, clamped to 0.72–1 × Impact.reach_of. Targets further away are reached by bending/leaning: the pivot moves up to BEND_MAX 0.95 m toward them.
- The edge lies along the radius, the head travels along the tangent. The cheeks open at the edge half-angle up to the eye thickness, and the haft trails behind.
- contact(): coarse key-point sweep, then fine 1 cm steps over edge, cheek and haft probes, then bisection. The first wood any probe touches stops the head. If a cheek or the haft touches first with no edge in the wood, the marker turns red ("jam").

Cut:
- The head goes on along the arc while σ·KAPPA/ETA·V(head∩wood) stays within the blow energy (Impact.wood's law on the real cut trunk). Cheeks in an open V cost nothing; cheeks against a narrow kerf cost a lot. Nothing goes past the eye, so no hole deeper than the head's own height.
- Removed wood = the head wedge at its stop + a chip prism. The chip splits along the grain toward the nearest free face (side/up rule). Its length is kl·depth·|n·grain|·PACE (PACE 2.0, the only fudge), capped at 2 × head length. A free face beside the chip within 1.5 × depth takes the strip between too.

Wood model (world/chop/wood_cuts.gd, WoodCuts):
- Convex pieces given as planes. Exact accounting by 5 mm slices along the grain, each touched slice a cell bitmap (3–7 mm cells; untouched slices are the analytic disk).
- Removed volume = cleared cells × cell volume, so chips equal removed wood to the cell.
- solid(p) is an O(1) bit test. A coarse 24×24 fibre mask per slice feeds the strength check: fibres intact over ±FIBRE_BAND carry the top; bending stress / MOR as before decides the fall.

ChopTree rewrite:
- apply_blow(flat planes, counts, point, into); the server sends pieces via rpc _tree_blow and every peer applies the same planes.
- The CSG is split into 0.15 m bands, 24 sectors, 8 pieces per group, so a blow redoes only the bands it reaches. The fall splits the band at the cut and moves the upper bands to the top body.
- `levels` now holds compact ChopModel section records (load, stress, fall_dir, hinge, cut_depth), same order on every peer. ## between them that went as chips beyond what the kerf had already chipped.
static func sever(rod: Dictionary, k: Dictionary) -> Dictionary:
	var ya: float = k.s - k.w * 0.5
	var yb: float = k.s + k.w * 0.5

	return {lo = lo, hi = hi, slab = frustum(rod, ya, yb) - float(k.taken)}


'''

open(p,'w').write(s)

Mechanics:
- **Wood:** a swing of any tool on a rod deepens a kerf with the same wood law as logs (Impact.wood, narrow-edge factor). The wood removed flies out as exact-volume chips. A rod cut through splits in two, and parts shorter than 12 cm become chips.
- **Support:** members stay up by touching the base plane, resting on a held member below, or (rails) being nailed to a held upright post. Whatever loses support becomes loose Timber, a RigidBody3D with the exact m3. A piece with nothing left is removed, and pieces standing on it (a roof on its wall) fall with it. The Timber is wood for building again: BuildSystem plans use it first, from its thin end, and it can be cut again.
- **Stone:** each hit gives off grit (Impact.rock crush volume) and adds loosening energy to the stone. It comes out when that energy passes friction times the weight of the stone plus those on it, times the slide distance. It then becomes a real StoneSystem chunk of the exact volume, and the stones above it fall.

A one-hand left swing uses the left shoulder and mirrors the direction.\n- The swing plane is spanned by shoulder→aim point and the camera right axis, turned by InputSystem.swing_of (wheel, 15° steps).\n- Radius = distance to what the look meets + DRIVE 4 cm, clamped to 0.72–1 × Impact.reach_of. Targets further away are reached by bending/leaning: the pivot moves up to BEND_MAX 0.95 m toward them.\n- The edge lies along the radius, the head travels along the tangent. The cheeks open at the edge half-angle up to the eye thickness, and the haft trails behind.\n- contact(): coarse key-point sweep, then fine 1 cm steps over edge, cheek and haft probes, then bisection. The first wood any probe touches stops the head. If a cheek or the haft touches first with no edge in the wood, the marker turns red (\"jam\").\n\nCut:\n- The head goes on along the arc while σ·KAPPA/ETA·V(head∩wood) stays within the blow energy (Impact.wood's law on the real cut trunk). Cheeks in an open V cost nothing; cheeks against a narrow kerf cost a lot. Nothing goes past the eye, so no hole deeper than the head's own height.\n- Removed wood = the head wedge at its stop + a chip prism. The chip splits along the grain toward the nearest free face (side/up rule). Its length is kl·depth·|n·grain|·PACE (PACE 2.0, the only fudge), capped at 2 × head length. A free face beside the chip within 1.5 × depth takes the strip between too.\n\nWood model (world/chop/wood_cuts.gd, WoodCuts):\n- Convex pieces given as planes. Exact accounting by 5 mm slices along the grain, each touched slice a cell bitmap (3–7 mm cells; untouched slices are the analytic disk).\n- Removed volume = cleared cells × cell volume, so chips equal removed wood to the cell.\n- solid(p) is an O(1) bit test. A coarse 24×24 fibre mask per slice feeds the strength check: fibres intact over ±FIBRE_BAND carry the top; bending stress / MOR as before decides the fall.\n\nChopTree rewrite:\n- apply_blow(flat planes, counts, point, into); the server sends pieces via rpc _tree_blow and every peer applies the same planes.\n- The CSG is split into 0.15 m bands, 24 sectors, 8 pieces per group, so a blow redoes only the bands it reaches.   "summary": "Tree part, task 52. Chopping is now a physical axe flight instead of \"the cut appears at the crosshair\".\n\nSwing (world/chop/axe_swing.gd, AxeSwing, pure and deterministic):\n- The head travels on a circle about the shoulder; crouching lowers the shoulder by Actor.CROUCH_DROP (binary meta, same on server, pilot and bots). A one-hand left swing uses the left shoulder and mirrors the direction.\n- The swing plane is spanned by shoulder→aim point and the camera right axis, turned by InputSystem.swing_of (wheel, 15° steps).\n- Radius = distance to what the look meets + DRIVE 4 cm, clamped to 0.72–1 × Impact.reach_of. Targets further away are reached by bending/leaning: the pivot moves up to BEND_MAX 0.95 m toward them.\n- The edge lies along the radius, the head travels along the tangent. The cheeks open at the edge half-angle up to the eye thickness, and the haft trails behind.\n- contact(): coarse key-point sweep, then fine 1 cm steps over edge, cheek and haft probes, then bisection. The first wood any probe touches stops the head. If a cheek or the haft touches first with no edge in the wood, the marker turns red (\"jam\").\n\nCut:\n- The head goes on along the arc while σ·KAPPA/ETA·V(head∩wood) stays within the blow energy (Impact.wood's law on the real cut trunk). Cheeks in an open V cost nothing; cheeks against a narrow kerf cost a lot. Nothing goes past the eye, so no hole deeper than the head's own height.\n- Removed wood = the head wedge at its stop + a chip prism. The chip splits along the grain toward the nearest free face (side/up rule). Its length is kl·depth·|n·grain|·PACE (PACE 2.0, the only fudge), capped at 2 × head length. A free face beside the chip within 1.5 × depth takes the strip between too.\n\nWood model (world/chop/wood_cuts.gd, WoodCuts):\n- Convex pieces given as planes. Exact accounting by 5 mm slices along the grain, each touched slice a cell bitmap (3–7 mm cells; untouched slices are the analytic disk).\n- Removed volume = cleared cells × cell volume, so chips equal removed wood to the cell.\n- solid(p) is an O(1) bit test. A coarse 24×24 fibre mask per slice feeds the strength check: fibres intact over ±FIBRE_BAND carry the top; bending stress / MOR as before decides the fall.\n\nChopTree rewrite:\n- apply_blow(flat planes, counts, point, into); the server sends pieces via rpc _tree_blow and every peer applies the same planes.\n- The CSG is split into 0.15 m bands, 24 sectors, 8 pieces per group, so a blow redoes only the bands it reaches. A cut to ≤3 % of a section (STUMP_SNAP) parts it: lower stump, wood above goes as chips, signal stump_cut. Return fresh copies — cd polus; python3 - <<'EOF'
p='world/chop/pine_mesh.gd'
s=open(p).read()
old='''## The arrays of a mesh built here (its CPU copy; a GPU read-back only for a mesh from elsewhere).
static func arrays_of(mesh: Mesh) -> Array:
	return mesh.get_meta(CPU_META) if mesh.has_meta(CPU_META) else mesh.surface_get_arrays(0)
'''
new='''## The arrays of a mesh built here: a fresh copy of its CPU arrays (packed arrays are shared by reference,
## callers append to them); a GPU read-back only for a mesh from elsewhere.
static func arrays_of(mesh: Mesh) -> Array:
	if not mesh.has_meta(CPU_META):
		return mesh.surface_get_arrays(0)
	var out: Array = (mesh.get_meta(CPU_META) as Array).duplicate()
	for i in out.size():
		if out[i] != null:
			out[i] = out[i].duplicate()
	return out
'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
s=s.replace("	var arr: Array = (mesh.get_meta(CPU_META) as Array).duplicate() if mesh.has_meta(CPU_META) else mesh.surface_get_arrays(0)\n	var verts: PackedVector3Array = (arr[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX] as PackedVector3Array).duplicate()",
 "	var arr := arrays_of(mesh)\n	var verts: PackedVector3Array = arr[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX]")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

**Fixes to make the parts work together**
- **First-cut stall in the browser removed.**

  - Fix: pine_mesh.gd now keeps a CPU copy of each mesh it builds (`_with_cpu`, `arrays_of`, which hands out fresh copies). valley_forest.gd and glade_forest.gd use that copy too, so trees streaming in on the valley no longer read meshes back either.
  - Result: the first blow went from 3161 ms to 55–157 ms.
